NYT Connections archive – All past answers

Every NYT Connections puzzle ever published is listed here, organised by date, with all four category groups and their sixteen words. The NYT only offers the current day’s puzzle for free, so this archive is the only place to find the answers to past games.

What the Archive Reveals About How Connections Works

In NYT Connections, you find four groups of four related words, colour-coded by difficulty: Yellow (easiest), Green, Blue, and Purple (hardest). Browsing the archive makes the puzzle’s design logic visible in a way that playing one puzzle a day never quite does.

The Yellow and Green categories tend to use surface-level associations, such as types of pasta, dog breeds, things found in a kitchen. 

The Blue and Purple categories are where the puzzle gets interesting and, occasionally, ruthless. Purple categories often involve wordplay, cryptic relationships, or obscure references requiring creative thinking. Looking back at past purples, a pattern emerges. The category title is almost always deceptively bland. “Words that follow FIRE” sounds straightforward but it isn’t.

The archive also exposes the puzzle’s favourite tricks. Words that seem to anchor an obvious group often belong somewhere else entirely. This is a classic misdirection the editors return to again and again. Spotting those traps in past puzzles is the fastest way to stop falling into them in future ones.

How to Use The Connections Archive

Browse by date to catch up on a puzzle you missed. Search by word if you remember one answer but not the category it belonged to. 

The puzzle is edited by crossword constructor Wyna Liu, and her sensibility runs through every past game in this archive. Study enough of them and you start to think the way she thinks. That’s when Connections stops being frustrating and starts being fun.
